html:
New South Wales was the oldest of the British colonies in Australia, shown on the map in 1880 and 1900, the last years before it became a state of the Commonwealth of Australia in 1901.

By then it was much smaller than the first colony of 1788. Victoria had been cut away in 1851 and Queensland in 1859. It had governed itself through an elected parliament since 1856. Sydney was a large port city, and wool from inland sheep stations, carried by new railways, was the main export. In 1883 silver was found at Broken Hill in the far west.

New South Wales favoured free trade, while Victoria protected its industries with tariffs, and the two colonies were rivals. Its premier Henry Parkes called for the colonies to unite in a speech at Tenterfield in 1889, and is remembered as the father of Federation. After conventions in the 1890s and votes in each colony, Federation came on 1 January 1901, during the long Federation Drought. To settle the rivalry, the new national capital was to be in New South Wales but well away from Sydney, at what became Canberra.
